title: K-flat quotient-projection comparison and coherent shifts
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$, and a finite-type $k$-scheme $W$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. On a fixed small skeleton $\mathcal V=W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ set $B_n=(R/t^n)_W$ for $n\ge1$ and $A=\lim_nB_n$. Let $\mathcal T$ be the ringed sequence site with ring $B=(B_n)_n$, and let $\mathscr S_W=\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal T}(B)$ be its strict quotient-semilinear module systems [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories and cochain shifts, with $d_{K[r]}=(-1)^r d_K$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix a supplied coefficient calculus $S$ with its coherence data, reduction $\mathcal R$ and total limit $\mathcal L=R\lim D(U)$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; $U$ is termwise scalar restriction along $A\to B_n$.

Let $p:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal T),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal V),A)$ be the ringed projection whose underlying inverse image is the constant-system functor $c$ and whose structural map $cA\to B$ consists of the quotient projections [def-pur-ringed-topos-morphism-of-universes].

The canonical universal left-derived comparison is a natural isomorphism $\alpha:Lp^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal R$ on $D(A)$. For every flat-term K-flat resolution $q:Q\to P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], both functors are identified with the same strict complex $(Q\otimes_A B_n)_n$, with transitions induced by $B_{n+1}\to B_n$. These identifications commute with maps of resolutions and their comparisons for a third resolution. After evaluation at every $n$ they are the canonical comparison with $P\otimes_A^LB_n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], without independently chosen finite resolutions or transitions.

For every integer $r$, $Q[r]$ is again K-flat with flat terms and $q[r]$ is a resolution. For any complex $T$ of $A$-modules the comparison
$$T\otimes_A Q[r]\xrightarrow{\sim}(T\otimes_A Q)[r]$$
is multiplication by $(-1)^{rp}$ on the summand $T^p\otimes_A Q^{q+r}$ of the direct-sum tensor total [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The pullback and finite scalar-extension shift comparisons on $Q[r]$ are the identity on $Q^{i+r}\otimes_A B_n$, with differential $(-1)^r(d_Q\otimes1)$. Thus $\alpha$ preserves these specified shift comparisons, on maps and on quotient transitions, naturally in all derived inputs. The comparisons respect shift zero, addition $r+s$ and inverse shifts using the usual cochain identifications. No flatness of $A\to B_n$, boundedness, completeness of $P$ or normalized-system hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Obtain the universal normalized counit for the supplied reduction from [lem-pur-sequence-reduction-universal]. Take L to be that very reduction and alpha to be its identity. The universal property implies uniqueness of any counit-compatible alpha by leftDerived_ext. This constructs the universal comparison data without choosing a second derived functor.

For a resolving Q choose its representative isomorphism, whose hom is pinned by the counit equation. For q:Q→P compose it with the inverse of reduction(Qq). Prefix by alpha_P for the pullback comparison. Counit naturality and qh=vqprime give both map squares after cancellation of reduction(Qq). Finite evaluation follows from the representative presentation and naturality of reductionEvaluation at Qq. The two- and three-resolution identities cancel alpha and adjacent isomorphisms. These are the Lean helper resolutionComparison.

Use the existing canonical mapBifunctorShift₂Iso for tensor with Q[r]. It identifies that tensor with a shift of the tensor with Q, so shift stability of acyclicity proves K-flatness. Flat terms reindex and the standard shifted quasi-isomorphism instance applies. The canonical CommShift on map₂CochainComplex supplies zero/addition coherence. Its summand inclusion formula gives (-1)^(rp) on the actual sheafified tensor generator, and NatTrans.shift_app_comm gives naturality in the first input.
Apply [lem-pur-sequence-reduction-shifts] to this universal comparison for its prescribed shift squares, and assemble the three conjuncts.
